report.tagline: India's largest site for comparing and buying insurance, backed by advisors who call you, explain plans and help you claim.
report.simpleSummary: PolicyBazaar lets you compare health, term life and car insurance from many companies in one place. Most Indians don't trust insurance and find it confusing, so PolicyBazaar has thousands of advisors who phone you, explain the plans and help you when you make a claim. Insurance companies pay PolicyBazaar a commission for every policy it sells, and again when you renew. Its parent, PB Fintech, also runs Paisabazaar for loans and credit cards.

overview.whatItDoes: PolicyBazaar is an insurance marketplace started in 2008. You enter a few details and see plans from most Indian insurers side by side, with price, cover and claim record. Advisors call to help you pick. After you buy, it reminds you to renew and helps when you claim. Insurers pay it a commission, so it is free for you.
howItWorks: You fill a short form: age, city, family members, and need (health, term life, car, bike, travel).
The site shows plans from many insurers with price, cover, waiting periods and claim settlement ratio.
An advisor calls within minutes to explain and answer questions; most sales close on this call.
You pay online; the money goes to the insurer, which issues the policy.
The insurer pays PolicyBazaar a commission, and more on each renewal.
When you claim, PolicyBazaar's claims team talks to the insurer and hospital on your behalf.
PB Partners lets local agents sell the same plans in smaller towns using PolicyBazaar's app.
overview.valueProposition: Pick the right policy at a fair price, without being pushed by one company's agent, and have someone on your side when you claim. For insurers: a cheap way to reach crores of buyers they could not reach through branches.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Shows plans from most insurers side by side with price and key terms.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Brings people in through Google and makes PolicyBazaar the starting point for insurance.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Trained advisors call leads to explain and close the sale.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Most Indians won't buy insurance without talking to someone. This is what turns visitors into buyers.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: A team that helps file claims and chases insurers.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: The main reason users trust PolicyBazaar over buying direct, and drives renewals.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: App for 5.5 lakh local agents to sell plans from many insurers.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Reaches small towns where people buy through someone they know.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Alerts and quick renewal before expiry.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Renewal commission is almost pure profit.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Compares loans and credit cards and shows free credit scores.

Sees ₹1 crore cover prices, roughly ₹1,000 to ₹1,500 a month for a 30-year-old non-smoker.
Advisor explains claim settlement ratios and riders.
Insurer arranges a home or lab test.
Policy appears in the account with renewal date.

Hospital sends request to the insurer.
Insurer asks for old reports; claims team helps.

businessModel.summary: PolicyBazaar is free for buyers. Insurers pay it a commission on each policy, plus fees for services like lead generation and tech. Renewals bring more commission at little cost. New businesses like PB Partners and PB Health add more revenue but have lower margins.

revenueStreams.detail: A share of the first-year premium, higher on health and term, plus smaller commission on renewals.
Fees for marketing, lead generation, tech and outsourced services.
Commission on policies sold by local agents, shared with those agents.
Fees from banks for loans and credit cards sold. Disbursals fell 80% in Q2 FY27 as lenders cut back.

businessModel.pricing: Free for users. Insurers set policy prices. Commissions follow IRDAI limits, and exact rates are not public.
costDrivers: Thousands of advisors and claims staff
Tech and AI tools for calls and support
businessModel.unitEconomics: Take one ₹20,000 health policy. PolicyBazaar may earn ₹3,000 to ₹5,000 in year one. Getting and closing that customer (ads plus advisor time) may cost ₹2,000 to ₹3,000. So the first sale makes a small profit. Each renewal then brings another commission at very little cost. A customer who stays five years is worth several times the first sale. These numbers are estimates.

howTheyGetUsers: Top Google rankings for insurance searches
PB Partners agents in small towns
whatBringsUsersBack: New needs like car, travel or parents' health
growth.moat: Brand trust, tie-ups with almost every insurer, and a large trained advisor and claims team. A plain comparison website can copy the listings, but not the people and the claims help built over 15+ years.

pmLessons: For low-trust products like insurance, a human on the phone can beat a perfect website.
Renewals turn a thin first sale into long-term profit, so design for the second year, not just the first.
A marketplace earns trust by showing choice and being on the user's side at claims time.
Growth tactics like heavy calling work, but they can wear down the brand.
To reach small towns, borrow the agent model and give agents better tools.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you cut spam calls without losing sales?
interviewQuestions.hint: Segment users, let them choose a channel, test WhatsApp and callbacks, and track conversion and complaints together.

interviewQuestions.question: Why does PolicyBazaar still use so many humans?
interviewQuestions.hint: Talk about trust, complex products, fear of claims, and how conversion changes with a call.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you raise health policy renewals?
interviewQuestions.hint: Find why people drop: price jumps, bad claims, forgetting. Fix each with reminders, claim help and cheaper plan options.

interviewQuestions.question: How should PolicyBazaar respond to Acko and Digit?
interviewQuestions.hint: Lean on choice, advice and claims help. Partner with them as insurers on the platform.

interviewQuestions.question: What should be the north star metric?
interviewQuestions.hint: Active policies kept or claims supported. Explain why first-year premium alone is wrong.
